                    ### Question
                    Six days after undergoing a thoracic endovascular aortic repair following a high-speed motorcycle accident, a 29-year-old woman develops a fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Serum studies show a sodium concentration of 129 mEq/L. An x-ray of the chest shows a left-sided pleural effusion. Thoracentesis is performed and shows milky white fluid in the pleural space that remains uniform after centrifugation. A culture of the pleural fluid shows no organisms. Further analysis of the fluid would most likely show which of the following?

                    ### Options
                    opa. High triglycerides
opb. Antinuclear antibodies
opc. High adenosine deaminase
opd. Cholesterol crystals
ope. High LDH

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The clinical presentation of fever, cough, shortness of breath, and a left-sided pleural effusion with milky white fluid after thoracic endovascular aortic repair suggests the development of a chylothorax, likely due to injury to lymphatic vessels. The uniformity of the fluid after centrifugation supports this diagnosis. Chylothorax is characterized by the presence of high triglycerides in the pleural fluid, which is consistent with the observed milky appearance. Therefore, the most likely finding in the pleural fluid analysis would be high triglycerides, aligning with the consensus that chylous effusions typically have elevated triglyceride levels.
